So what's your favourite Bond movie and/or actor
[Discussion] Keeping up with the Bond themed news I've been posting I wanted to ask what everyone's favourite Bond movie is.

I'm actually going to have to go with skyfall. I've loved everything about Craig's Bond but I feel like this is where everything came together so well and changed everything. First off it of course a very well directed and beautiful movie. It also has one of the best Bond villains we have seen in a long time which is something that's been missing for a while. And of course I have to mention it finally added a Q again which we haven't had for so long

I liked Skyfall until I saw a CinemaSins type of video about it where a lot of things were pointed out about it that made no sense (I don't think it was a CinemaSins video but it was similar to one). When I rewatched it I saw there was a lot of terrible writing and some continuity errors that made me question how I hadn't noticed it the first time. My favourite one is probably either Casino Royale or From Russia With Love. I don't go to the cinema that often, but I went to see Casino Royale when it came out and was blown away, although it was probably because I'd just suffered through 4 Pierce Brosnan Bond films.

I'll admit the movie had its problems, especially with the plot. The drive he actually heads out to get is almost completely forgotten by the end of the movie, Silva's escape literally makes no sense. But I feel like that ending scene in skyfall as well as having Ralph Fiennes take over as M really make up for it. Casino Royale is a close second mainly because it's the first time we see this completely new Bond

I love his escape. Not only did he know exactly where to go once he escaped, he had already been there to plant an explosive and timed it exactly so the tube would come through the wall. I know the Bond films are supposed to be fun films so maybe I'm just reading into it too much. My favourite Bond film mistake has to be the one where he's driving a car on a beach and the tyres make screeching sounds, can't remember which film it was though.

The tube is actually the worst part. From the way it was shown Silva didn't know that part of the chase was going to happen. But yet somehow he knew the exact place to set the charge and knew the exact moment the train would be there seemingly months ahead of time

Skyfall. I'm not a big fan of the old campy James Bond movies. I prefer the more gritty, realistic, and brutal versions, even if they don't feel like "Bond Movies". The old ones were a product of their time, but they wouldn't work in modern box offices.

I agree the old ones very much were a product of their time. We saw what happens when we try and bring that style into the new century with movies like Die Another Day. Then Craig stepped up with Casino Royale which really changed everything but I fee like skyfall was really the one to perfect the new Bond style
